newsitem.title: USA: Fla. sees case against tobacco aided by settlement.
newsitem.headline: Fla. sees case against tobacco aided by settlement.

text.p: An attorney assisting Florida in a lawsuit seeking RICO damages from the tobacco industry said Thursday he expected the case to be bolstered by Liggett Group's settlement of tobacco lawsuits with 22 states.
As part of the settlement, Liggett, owned by Bennet LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd, will turn over material, including internal documents and attorney-client correspondence.

"(The documents) validate our RICO allegations that this was a concerted effort to deceive the public and addict our children and hide the evidence," the Florida attorney, Tim Howard, told Reuters after a news conference following the announcement of the Liggett settlement.
Howard also said that, as the case progresses over the next few weeks, his team would be deposing a number of prominent physicians in preparation for a trial expected to begin this summer.

In the lawsuit filed in West Palm Beach, Fla., the state is using provisions of the Florida Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) act, which is similar to the federal statute of the same name, to enhance its claim the tobacco industry should reimburse it for more than $1 billion spent to provide health care for people with tobacco-related illnesses.
If Florida were to win its claims against tobacco companies under the RICO Act, the damages it is seeking could be tripled to more than $3 billion and set a precedent for other states.
